meta.what: The daemon feature matrix: each boot-path program, how Apple ships it in 27.0.1, how it runs on the furthest 27-only configuration, and its state.

apple_27.arm64e only: 27.0.1 ships this program for Apple silicon only

runs_as.lifted: Apple's 27.0.1 arm64e program recompiled to x86_64 by the project's lifter, linked against 27's x86_64 libraries
runs_as.translated: Apple's 27.0.1 arm64e program run as itself through the kernel's foreign-architecture exec route, with a user-space translator as its engine
runs_as.borrowed from 26: an x86_64 build of the same program from macOS 26 (Tahoe), a temporary bridge
runs_as.stand-in: a small script the project wrote in its place

states.done: runs as 27's own code and was seen working
states.in progress: a bridge is used, or 27's code runs with a known wall

programs.note: All 1,468 functions lifted, 1,403 pass the differential test, 0 fail. In one boot the kernel's code-directory hash for pid 1 equals the lift's, proving which launchd ran. Not yet folded into a disk image. Stopping a service no longer panics the guest: 0 panics in 2 boots with the fix, against 1 in a control boot without it.
100 of 100 functions lifted, 99 pass. 0 environment errors in 1,020 job spawns; macOS 26's xpcproxy fails beside 27's launchd.

Stays up, exit status 0, in 4 boots, where macOS 26's amfid crashes in every boot. In one boot it refused an ad hoc signed program carrying a restricted entitlement, with Apple's error for that case; an edited-signature test did not discriminate.

27's own logd runs translated as the logd job on the furthest configuration, exit status 0 in 3 of 3 boots; in one, the kernel's code-directory hash for it equals Apple's arm64e build. 27's log command reading its messages back was measured on other configurations (2 of 2), not yet on this one.

27's own logd_helper runs translated on the furthest configuration, exit status 0 in 3 of 3 boots; in one, the kernel's code-directory hash for it equals Apple's arm64e build. Doing its job is not measured.

Died at boot when launchd started it, before patch X. With X, a hand-started copy got past the failure in 2 of 2 boots; in the second, the launchd-started copy was still restarting, though that copy ran with a trace option the hand-started one did not, so the two are not a controlled comparison. That fix (patch X) had an open race and has been replaced by patch Y, whose boots are not written up in this record yet.
Not started in the boot measured (on demand).

Starts and checks in. The 240-second registry stall it reported is explained (docs/gaps.md, B18): with either measured fix, 0 stall lines in every test boot counted. Neither fix is in the furthest configuration yet.
Run to rc 0 in the guest, but rc 0 was not a load: a kext was not loaded afterwards. Collections are still built by macOS 26's kmutil.
Started in debug mode by a test payload, not by launchd. With a 180 s login timeout, 3 of 3 logins in 8 of 9 boots and 1 of 3 in one; with a 60 s timeout, none (docs/components.md).

603 functions pass, 0 fail. Relinked with the newer link tools, on a root with the registry stall fixed, it ran the whole boot and both disk rounds (a scratch disk and a RAM disk) passed through it (1 boot). Earlier, in one image, its clients got no answer from it, lifted or translated. Apple's own arm64e build under translation served the scratch-disk round in 7 of 8 boots counted with the registry quiet.
726 functions pass, 0 fail. Runs for the whole boot. Under translation it needed the translator to count its own memory against the process limit.

38 of 38 functions pass. Serves for the whole boot. It creates the root of the system's per-user temporary folders itself, so the copy the project used to pre-create on the image is retired (2 of 2 boots).
Boot task. The real work is in 27's x86_64 fsck_apfs, which it calls.
Boot task. An early kernel panic at its exit was traced to the borrowed macOS 26 Sandbox kext, not to this program; the recompiled 27 Sandbox kext does not have it.
Boot task. Calls 27's x86_64 corecrypto.
Boot task (data protection), run to success. The prngseedd job label, which uses the same program, did not start in the boot counted in docs/launchd-labels.md.
Placed; launchd runs it as a boot task, but whether the task succeeds has not been read. Its job label did not start in the boot counted in docs/launchd-labels.md.
Boot tasks and tools; run to success.

Exited with status 74 about every 10 s, at an indirect call into a lazy-load helper section the link tools did not translate. Relinked with the newer link tools, it ran once for the whole boot with 0 such exits (1 boot). What it does is not read.
A 945-byte shell script that runs 27's own x86_64 apfs_boot_util. Lifting 27's mount would retire it.

programs.note: Running. Doing their job is measured only for configd (a DHCP address) and the shells.

Starts under translation on the 27-only root. In one boot it never opened the framebuffer; in 6 later boots, with the two display byte edits placed in the root's cache, it stayed up, 5 of them showed the boot progress window, and none showed a login window (docs/components.md). The graphics stack it starts (SkyLight) does ship x86_64.

Measured on one boot of a later overlay of the 27-only root, signed as a bundle with the lab key: it launches, then exits with status 70 every time (236 starts, 236 exits, no crash report). The cause of status 70 is not read. On the display test overlays 27's arm64e loginwindow runs translated instead and keeps running through the observed boots (3 read); in one boot it logged that it had registered for the notification that the login window was shown.
Planned as 27's own programs.

programs.program: Apple HID driver extension (keyboard and tablet services)
programs.n: 1 boot crashing read in full, 3 with the fix, and a static reading
programs.note: Apple's HID driver extension (com.apple.AppleUserHIDDrivers) ships an x86_64 slice, which runs against 27's x86_64 DriverKit shared cache. It crashed at start with SIGBUS before any driver code ran, and was launched again and again (6 launches and 17 crash lines in one boot; 6 and 5 crash reports in two boots of later overlays). Cause, read statically from 27.0.1's own files: that cache's libdyld forwards calls to dyld one table slot short, so a call reaches the neighbouring function, which writes into a read-only code page. With the shifted forwarding stubs moved up one slot and the cache re-signed, it launched once and was not relaunched (2 boots read), no crash line named it (3 boots on two overlays), and both HID event services started (1 boot read in full). Keyboard and mouse input does not work yet.
